exposure: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) severity (mild, moderate, severe)
cohort: The study included 215 women diagnosed with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) based on pruritus and bile acid levels >=10 mmol/L, recruited between January 2005 and August 2012.
finding: Higher bile acid levels in women with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy were significantly associated with spontaneous preterm birth, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, and perinatal death, and maternal and fetal BA levels were positively correlated.
